sector_model: vertical SaaS plus payments and screening (usage-based value-added services, SBC-adjusted cash flow, net cash, buybacks); not a bank/insurer/REIT model
thesis: AppFolio sells property-management software and payments, tenant screening and resident services. Q3 2026 revenue 295.7M (+19%), 9M 839.0M (+19%): subscription +15%, value added services +22% (payments, screening, risk mitigation), units under management +8%. 9M income from operations 161.1M vs 109.3M, net income 129.9M (+28.7%), OCF 218.7M, no debt, cash and short-term securities 307.3M plus 87.7M long-term investments, 9M buybacks 129.2M. At the verified 2026-11-09 close 229.49 and 35.456M Class A plus Class B shares the market cap is about 8.1B: 47.9x TTM GAAP net income, 3.4% FCF yield (2.5% after stock compensation). A high-quality grower priced for continued 15-20% growth; not obviously mispriced.
counterthesis: Growth rests on value-added services (78% of 9M revenue), which are usage-driven and depend on payments, screening volumes and attach rates, not just unit count (+8%). The effective tax rate rose to 22% in 9M26 from 12.5% in 9M25 (valuation allowance/credits normalising), so earnings growth overstates pre-tax trend: pre-tax income grew 44.7% but net income only 28.7%, and TTM P/E remains about 48x. Q3 operating margin 19.4% depends on S&M staying contained (S&M +35% in Q3). SBC is 7% of revenue, and net share settlement plus buybacks consume cash. Competition from Yardi, RealPage, Buildium and AI-native entrants, regulatory scrutiny of tenant screening and fees, and a weak rental or housing market are not quantified here.
invalidation: Value-added services growth slowing below about 10%, units under management growth falling or churn rising, operating margin falling below mid-teens, rising regulatory limits on screening or payment fees, or net income growth stalling while the shares still trade above 40x earnings.
